question: When can observed servicing histories support a decision about a repeated intervention despite dropout?
kind: Generated study, no bank data or observed bank performance
law: X~N(0,1); L0=.4X+eps0; three actions; p(A=1)=clip(expit(.3X-.5L+.2Aprev),lo,hi); Lnext=.6L+.25X-.5A+eps; R=10-2Lnext^2-A+.5AX
censoring: After A but before next-state/reward observation: g=.65+.30expit(.3L-.2A); observation dropout is absorbing. In the invalid case the logit additionally includes 1.5*eps_next, unavailable to the analyst.
selected_policy: Choose one of the four thresholds using known-law prefix-IPW value on 2000 separate training trajectories; freeze for independent evaluation.
target: Expected sum of the three rewards under the policy intervention for the generated population, without conditioning on remaining observed

estimators.prefix_ipw: For each reward use product of action match/probability and observed censoring/probability through that time; average total score over all initial trajectories.
estimators.complete_case: Unweighted total reward among fully observed trajectories whose entire action sequence matches the policy; deliberately biased practitioner comparison.
estimators.fitted_gcomp: Fit pooled Lnext on intercept,L,X,A using only observed transitions; estimate innovation variance; simulate policy trajectories under fitted Gaussian dynamics. Reward rule is supplied by this constructed study. No confidence interval claimed for this plug-in method.

uncertainty: Normal interval for independent trajectory-level prefix scores; reference value has its own Monte Carlo SE. Coverage against numerical reference is reported with Monte Carlo uncertainty and near-boundary ambiguity. No exact or universal guarantee.
metrics: Bias, RMSE and average interval width
Point-reference coverage, MC SE and ambiguous reference-boundary count
Mean and minimum prefix effective sample sizes, maximum weights
Paired value difference vs always-zero, conditional selected-policy regret to the finite candidate set
Availability of every estimator including empty complete-case samples
review: Targets and initial cohorts match; complete-case targets a selected group and is labelled. Selection uses separate training data. Reference potential trajectories are evaluator-only. g-computation omits a state predictor only in the predeclared adverse case. Equal observed point performance does not establish empirical superiority. No honest uncertainty claim is made for g-computation without a parameter-uncertainty calculation.
promotion_criterion: A useful conditional scientific conclusion and reproducible diagnostics; this small Monte Carlo exercise does not qualify bank deployment.
promotion_veto: Incorrect target, unavailable interval or unsupported observation mechanism prevents stronger claims, but does not stop the next scenario.
continuation_veto: Nonfinite/corrupt numerical outputs, missing required score diagnostics or compute budget exceeded.
interpretation: Generated reward units; costs already enter reward. No actual dollars, general policy optimality, hidden-state identification or bank ROI.
